I don't have `reference/scene.md` or `reference/layout.md` loaded in this session (only the genre-independent core doc above), so I can't verify the exact block/edge/pin spellings against their authoritative source. I've composed the figure from what the core grammar guarantees — quoted labels, bare ids, `class` for meaning, `layout`/`pin` as the only layout-zone directive — and used `pin` to fix the one edge's route through the two waypoints, since that's exactly what the layout zone is for: geometry to stabilize the render against a future addition, carrying no meaning of its own.

```figdown
# FigDown — figures as text. Spec: https://github.com/FigDown/figdown
figdown 0.1 block
title "Alert-forwarding chain"

class svc "Internal service" fill=#e0f2fe stroke=#0284c7

block probe "Probe" class=svc
block normalizer "Normalizer" class=svc
block sink "Sink" class=svc

edge probe -> normalizer
edge normalizer -> sink

layout
pin probe->normalizer at (60,20) (90,40)
```

Notes:
- `probe`, `normalizer`, `sink` are the three services with short labels only — no extra prose crammed into the blocks, per the "keep labels short" guidance.
- The `probe -> normalizer` edge is pinned through `(60,20)` then `(90,40)` so it visibly jogs, leaving room for the future third element; this lives in the layout zone and carries no semantic claim.
- Before committing this, run `node <skill-dir>/build-svg.js` against it — if `block`/`edge`/`pin` turn out to be spelled differently in `reference/scene.md`/`reference/layout.md`, the build will fail with a `Line N:` error naming the correct keyword, and the fix is mechanical from there.
